title: Modbus request/response you can break on purpose
objective: Implement Modbus TCP ADU for function 0x03 and 0x06, return exception 0x02 on an unmapped address, show MBAP length matching the PDU, and run at least 20 generated cases.
whyThisMatters: A PLC map is not JSON. If you cannot hex-dump an MBAP header and an illegal-address exception, you will debug plant integrations by guessing. This task uses the official Modbus application protocol spec on the host — no licensed stack, no hardware gateway.
evidence: Server and client C (or C server plus a documented test client) with incremental Git history
A captured hex dump of a 0x03 read of holding registers 0..3 after those registers were written, showing request and response
A captured hex dump of a read of an unmapped address returning exception function 0x83 and exception code 0x02
A note or dump showing the MBAP length field equals the PDU size plus the remaining MBAP rule in the spec for both captured frames
A captured run of at least 20 generated (property) cases with a pass count
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: A client read of holding registers 0 through 3 returns the values previously written with function 0x06 (or 0x10 if you also implement it); request and response hex dumps are captured.
A read of an address outside the implemented map returns function code 0x83 and exception code 0x02; the hex dump is captured.
For both the success and exception frames, the MBAP Length field is consistent with the PDU size as defined in the Modbus TCP ADU (Length = remaining bytes after the Length field).
A property or generated-case suite of at least 20 cases runs in one command; the captured output prints a pass count greater than or equal to 20.
